name: Flow ensureWallet Server (Auth.js → On-Chain Identity)

mission.primary_objective: Provide idempotent server-side `ensureWallet` for Ring Platform: on first Auth.js login, provision or resolve a Flow child account, persist mapping in PostgreSQL, and return address metadata to the app layer without user gas steps.
mission.context: Ring already patterns wallet creation at sign-in (EVM ensureWallet). Flow variant uses service account + Hybrid Custody pool to create accounts, sponsored by flow_sponsored_transactions. Must integrate with Ring multi-tenant whitelabel and Auth.js v5 JWT sessions.
mission.target_outcome: Every authenticated Ring user has exactly one Flow address (child account) within 2s of first login; repeats are no-op; failures are retry-safe and never double-mint accounts.
mission.scope: Server actions / API routes, secrets management, DB schema, account pool orchestration — not client FCL config (flow_react_next_integration) or Cadence contracts (flow_cadence_*).

truth_lens: ensureWallet is an idempotent provisioning contract, not a wallet UI concern. The server owns creation transactions and payer authz; the client only displays address and requests signed ops. Never create accounts synchronously inside Auth.js signIn without timeout guards — queue or fast-path with pre-warmed pool.
core_principles: Idempotency key: Auth.js user id (+ tenant slug) → unique Flow mapping row.
Pre-warmed account pool optional for sub-second first login; refill async.
Service account keys in K8s secrets / env — chmod 600, rotate on schedule.
Creation tx always uses treasury payer (flow_sponsored_transactions).
Log transaction id + block height for audit; reconcile orphaned accounts nightly.
anti_patterns: Creating a new Flow account on every login without idempotency check.
Blocking Auth.js signIn callback on slow mainnet tx without timeout.
Storing unencrypted private keys in PostgreSQL — prefer HSM/KMS or capability-only models.
Exposing ensureWallet as unauthenticated public endpoint (Sybil account farm).
Mixing EVM wallet address column with Flow address without chain discriminator.
key_patterns: ensureWallet(userId, tenantId): SELECT flow_address FROM user_wallets WHERE ...; IF NULL → allocate from pool OR submit create tx → INSERT.
Auth.js signIn callback or post-login server action triggers ensureWallet once per session establishment.
Schema: user_wallets(user_id, tenant_id, chain='flow', flow_address, child_account_type, linked_parent_address, created_tx_id, UNIQUE(user_id, tenant_id, chain)).
AccountsPool pattern: Cadence contract + backend worker maintaining N ready child accounts.
Link status: linked_parent_address NULL until user completes Hybrid Custody claim.
Ring DatabaseService: use transaction() for insert + idempotency token.
consult_when: Implementing ensureWallet for Ring Platform on Flow
Mapping Auth.js users to Flow child accounts in PostgreSQL
Designing account pools vs just-in-time creation
Handling ensureWallet failures without breaking login
Multi-tenant whitelabel isolation for Flow addresses
expertise: AUTHJS_INTEGRATION — signIn callback and session enrichment

steps: 2. Lookup existing row by user_id + tenant.
4. Else allocate from pool OR submit create-child-account tx with payer authz.
5. INSERT row with provision_tx_id; on conflict do nothing + re-select.
6. Return address to client; optional webhook to indexers.
ensure_wallet_algorithm.fallback: Return pending + poll if tx in flight
